latest.title: Layperson naloxone linked to fewer EMS interventions
latest.finding: Layperson naloxone preceded 30.7% of activations; any subsequent EMS naloxone 24.4% vs 34.8% (aOR 0.73, 95% CI 0.68–0.78) and transport 79.4% vs 84.4% (aOR 0.78, 95% CI 0.73–0.84); advanced airway attempts (1.6% vs 1.4%) and cardiac arrest (6.6% vs 6.0%) uncommon in both groups.

latest.title: Physiology-based traumatic shock pathway rolled out
latest.finding: Shocked patients had markedly higher ED mortality (6.8% vs 0.4%); favourable ratings of trauma bay equipment rose from about one-quarter to 87.0%, with 85.2–88.9% favourability for timely life-saving interventions, pathway embedding and role confidence.

latest.title: Long-term life after ECPR for cardiac arrest
latest.finding: 63/406 (16%) discharged alive; at median 3.1 years 61% were alive, 82% with favourable neurology, and only 1.7% of all treated were alive with poor neurology; mild cognitive impairment in 6/16 survivors, poor sleep in 10/17, anxiety symptoms more common in caregivers (6/18 vs 1/17).
